requirement:
When loading a supported legacy evidence record that did not capture its
procedure version, Habeas represents that missing version as `*`.
In-place conversion preserves this wildcard rather than assigning the current
version. The wildcard matches any
requested review revision under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records.procedure_match`.
The record is current when its recorded inputs and all existing application
freshness checks still match. Version matching leaves the subject, reference-set,
input, determination, citation, and site checks intact.

For new assessments, Habeas's validation value supplies a concrete review revision
other than `*`, and the assessment records it.
rationale:
I judged the reviewed tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_conversion.legacy_freshness`. I did not request implementation source. I did not assess the cited `procedure_match` requirement's own tests.

The requirement breaks into five obligations. Each has a test that asserts its outcome.

1. **A legacy record without a procedure version loads as `*`.**
   - `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[legacy_conversion_preserves_every_historical_field_without_resolving_sources]` decodes legacy records for a definition, a citation and a site. It asserts `record.revision == "*"`, and that the native encoding's `review_version` is `*`.
   - `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once]` loads legacy files through `load_evidence` for all four review kinds. It asserts `loaded.revision == "*"`, and that the dependencies and output match the decoded record.

2. **In-place conversion keeps the wildcard.**
   - `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[current_legacy_authoring_converts_without_configuration_and_stdout_never_converts]` runs authoring over an existing legacy file with no configuration. The converted file has `review_version == "*"`, and its `view` equals the old record.
   - The same test shows stdout output never converts. The file is unchanged and no extra files are left behind.

3. **`*` matches any requested revision.**
   - `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[native_freshness_checks_versions_inputs_and_application_fields]` checks that a `*` record is current under `"future-review-version"`.
   - In the same test, a concrete `old-concrete-version` record is not current under `REVIEW_VERSION`. This confirms only `*` acts as a wildcard.

4. **The record is current when its inputs and application checks match, and version matching leaves those checks intact.**
   - The "every review kind" test shows legacy and native `*` files produce no findings when nothing has changed.
   - It then applies one semantic mutation at a time, with the version still `*`. Each mutation must be reported, and the native conversion must produce identical findings.
     - Every kind: a false determination, and a changed input hash or text.
     - Definition: changed subject text, and a changed reference-set hash.
     - Citation: a different `file`, a different `item`, and changed citation commentary.
     - Site: a different requirement, file or item; changed queries; changed fixmes; and `applies` set to false.
   - Each mutated record still loads, so staleness is reported as a finding and not as a loading error.
   - The `native_freshness_checks_versions_inputs_and_application_fields` test also shows a `*` record becomes stale when the requirement text changes.

5. **New assessments record a concrete revision other than `*`.**
   - `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[authoring_keeps_the_prepared_subject_snapshot_and_concrete_version]` asserts `review_version == REVIEW_VERSION` and `!= "*"`.
   - The same test decodes the record. It confirms the record is stale (`record_is_current` is false) once the source has changed.

Every test carrying a reference to this requirement is marked `{test}`, so there are no marking gaps. I found no obligation, boundary or failure case without a test and an asserting check.

// Defined in habeas_sdk::graph.
/// Compare the saved review-rule revision with the currently requested revision.
pub fn procedure_matches(stored: &str, requested: &str) -> bool;
The revision matches when the stored `Record::revision` is `*` or equals the
requested revision exactly. Only the complete stored value `*` is a wildcard;
other values compare literally. A wildcard leaves dependency comparison and
result decoding unchanged. It matches revisions for the selected source and
criterion only, and does not supply evidence for other criteria.
